title: The Pessoa Knowledge Graph: A Federated Linked-Data Representation of the Heteronymic System (EA-PKG-01) v1.0
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
EA-PKG-01 launches a proposed federated linked-data representation of Fernando Pessoa’s heteronymic system. The project targets Wikidata as its primary substrate and defines a bounded build including Pessoa, approximately seventy-two cataloged authorial figures, attributed works, publication venues, institutions, contemporaries, influences, downstream reception, places, and theoretical concepts. It requires English, Brazilian Portuguese, and Portuguese labels, scholarly references, and explicit relation modeling.

The launch document identifies three intended repairs: a fuller open inventory, encoded relations among heteronyms, and preservation of typological differences. It supplies source priorities, phase planning, predicate guidance, collaboration procedures, and a projected dedicated visualization. It is a foundational plan, not evidence that all target nodes and references were completed. Claims about the condition of Wikidata and the exact number of existing items belong to the April 2026 audit surface.

wiki_article:
**The Pessoa Knowledge Graph** is a linked-data project launched by Lee Sharks to represent Fernando Pessoa’s heteronymic system in federated open infrastructure. The foundational document is designated EA-PKG-01.

The proposed graph includes Pessoa, chief and minor heteronyms, semi-heteronyms, proto-heteronyms, para-heteronyms, pseudonyms, works, magazines, institutions, collaborators, places, literary influences, downstream reception, and concepts such as sensationism and orthonymy. Its central design principle is that Pessoa’s authorial types and internal relations must be machine-queryable rather than compressed into one undifferentiated list.

The project uses Wikidata as the principal public substrate and calls for multilingual labels, structured scholarly references, correct work-to-heteronym attribution, and links to primary archives and critical editions. The document also proposes a later public visualization and a broader lineage map connecting Pessoa with other heteronymic practices. EA-PKG-01 is a launch and governance record: it defines scope, standards, and intended phases, while the companion implementation document inventories concrete edits and the later typology and synthesis papers supply the theoretical model.
